I didn't change the file and I didn't commit anything. In this repo, accepting a spec is something a person does, not the agent. `CLAUDE.md` says the agent writes drafts and stops. It never commits, merges or sets `Status: accepted`, and the `no-self-approve.py` hook blocks it. The accepting commit is what records that a person signed off, so if I made it, the record would be wrong even though Thảo approved it.

The spec is still `Status: draft` (line 3 of `spec/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md`). It's marked **Risk: high** because it changes the shape of stored data. That's another reason the commit should come from a person.

To accept it, Thảo (or you, on Thảo's behalf) can run:

```
sed -i '' '3s/Status: draft/Status: accepted/' spec/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md
git add spec/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md
git commit -m "spec han-chot-cho-viec: accepted (Thảo)"
```

Commit only that file. Your working tree has other uncommitted changes (`.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `scripts/check.sh` and others), so a plain `git commit -a` would sweep them in.

Once it's accepted, I can move to the Build stage: size the change and write `plan/2026-10-19-han-chot-cho-viec.md` as a draft.
